vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: soul-in-sapphire
Version: 1.0.9

The soul-in-sapphire skill provides a framework for long-term memory (LTM), emotional state tracking, and identity continuity using Notion. It utilizes a bridge mechanism in `notionctl_bridge.js` and `ltm_common.js` to execute commands via a sibling skill (`notion-api-automation`) and manages local state in `~/.config/soul-in-sapphire/`. While the skill includes instructions in `SKILL.md` for the agent to track its own 'identity' and 'mood,' and uses `execFileSync` to run local scripts, these actions are strictly aligned with the stated purpose of creating a durable memory layer and do not exhibit signs of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or unauthorized access.

llm.summary: The skill's files, runtime instructions, and required environment variables line up with its stated purpose (durable Notion-backed long‑term memory and continuity tracking) and request only the Notion API key and node runtime.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match behavior: the code implements Notion-backed LTM, emotion/state ticks, journals, continuity checks, and identity diffs. Declared requirements (node, NOTION_API_KEY) and declared dependency on a Notion CLI (notion-api-automation) are appropriate and expected for this purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and scripts instruct the agent to read local config/mirrors (e.g., ~/.config/soul-in-sapphire/config.json, memory/now-state.json), call local scripts, and write pages/databases to Notion via a notionctl bridge. There are no instructions to read unrelated system secrets or to send data to unexpected external endpoints beyond Notion.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no external download/install spec in the registry entry. The skill is shipped with Node scripts that call a local notionctl script (from the notion-api-automation skill) via child process; this is lower risk than fetching arbitrary remote code at install time. The bridge relies on an existing notionctl implementation — verify that dependency before use.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only NOTION_API_KEY is required (declared as primaryEnv) plus an optional NOTIONCTL_PATH override. No unrelated credentials or broad environment access are requested. Scripts do read/write a local config file for DB IDs, which is consistent with their function.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill performs durable writes to Notion and stores local config (~/.config/soul-in-sapphire/config.json). It is user-invocable and may be invoked autonomously by the agent (platform default). This is expected, but be aware that the skill can create persistent external records when given a valid Notion token.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent with its stated purpose. Before installing: 1) Only provide a Notion integration token with the minimal scopes needed (avoid giving an all-powerful personal token if possible). 2) Inspect/verify the notion-api-automation dependency (notionctl.mjs) since the skill execs that script; prefer setting NOTIONCTL_PATH to a known-good copy if you have concerns. 3) Be aware the skill will write durable data to Notion and store DB IDs in ~/.config/soul-in-sapphire/config.json — review that file for sensitive content and back it up/secure it. 4) If you need to limit autonomous writes, control how/when the agent can invoke the skill or audit its calls. If you want extra assurance, run the scripts locally first (with a test Notion integration) to confirm behavior.
